rows.title: Triple Screen Trading System
rows.original_creator_claim_cached: Alexander Elder's Triple Screen Trading System improves trading entries by aligning trend-following indicators and momentum oscillators across three timeframes.; Using a timeframe ratio of 3 to 5 (e.g., Weekly, Daily, 4-Hour) filters out false signals and improves timing relative to corrections.; Combining a 100 Hull Moving Average on the high timeframe, RSI on the tactical timeframe, and price action/trendline breakouts on the execution timeframe reduces risk.; Multi-timeframe systems isolate responsibilities: high timeframe handles directional bias (context layer), mid-timeframe measures pullback timing (filter layer), and low timeframe handles entry timing (execution layer).; Timeframe scaling factors (3x-5x) provide a structured approach to temporal filtering without over-sampling intra-bar noise.
rows.limitations: Subject to lag from moving average calculations and lookahead bias if higher timeframe bar completion times are not properly aligned in execution code.; Fixed RSI levels like 50 can generate frequent false breaks during sideways/ranging market regimes.; Claims that following multi-timeframe confluence surely reduces the risk of bad entries without empirical statistical validation.; Visual demonstration relies on hand-picked historical chart segments with discretionary trendline and pattern annotations.; No performance metrics, backtest statistics, execution friction (spreads, slippage, commissions), or funding rate costs are provided.; High-view YouTube material is hypothesis-only and never proves alpha or profitability.

rows.original_creator_claim_cached: These four backtesting rules form the exact backbone used by institutional quant firms like Renaissance Technologies and Susquehanna to scale automated portfolios.; Applying these four backtesting techniques will separate real edges from statistical noise and prevent strategy failure in live markets.; Validation pipelines must evaluate strategy parameter stability across adjacent parameter ranges (heatmaps) to detect overfitting cliffs.; Walk-forward optimization must enforce strict out-of-sample data splits to verify generalization across temporal regimes.; System stress testing should evaluate performance under artificially inflated friction (higher commissions, elevated slippage, and signal execution delays).; Monte Carlo trade-sequence reshuffling isolates sequence risk and provides realistic drawdown distributions independent of single historical equity paths.
